scenes.problem: Two square picture frames have areas 36 cm² and 64 cm². How many centimetres longer is the larger perimeter?
rows: Each area is the side multiplied by itself: s₁²=36, s₂²=64.
Find the first side: √36=6 cm; a 6 by 6 square has area 36.
Find the second side: √64=8 cm; a 8 by 8 square has area 64.
The first perimeter is 4 × 6 = 24 cm.
The second perimeter is 4 × 8 = 32 cm.
Subtract perimeters: 32 − 24 = 8 cm.
scenes.misconception: Find both sides from their areas, then compare linear perimeters, not areas.

scenes.problem: Two cubic boxes have volumes 27 cm³ and 125 cm³. How much longer is one edge of the larger box?
rows: A cube has three equal edges; V=s³.
Take ∛27=3 cm, because 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.
Take ∛125=5 cm, because 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
Compare edge lengths rather than subtracting volumes.
Subtract 5 − 3 = 2 cm.
scenes.misconception: Find both cube roots before comparing edge lengths; keep cubic and linear units separate.

scenes.problem: One square display has side 2³ cm; another has area 100 cm². Find the difference between their areas.
rows: First evaluate the given side: 2³=8 cm.
Square that side to get the first area: 8 × 8=64 cm².
The other display already has area 100 cm².
Its side would be √100=10 cm; check 10²=100.
Subtract the smaller area from the larger: 100−64=36 cm².
scenes.misconception: A side written as a power must be evaluated, then squared to obtain its area.

scenes.problem: Compare 2⁴ with √81 × ∛8. By how much do the two values differ?
rows: Keep the power on the left and product of roots on the right.
Evaluate the left: 2⁴ = 16.
Evaluate √81 = 9; 9² = 81.
Evaluate ∛8 = 2; 2³ = 8.
Multiply the right: 9 × 2 = 18.
Compare 16 and 18; difference = 18 − 16 = 2.
scenes.misconception: Evaluate each power and root before comparing the two complete sides.

scenes.problem: Two square garden beds have areas 36 m² and 64 m². A cubic planter has volume 27 m³. Find the sum of both bed perimeters and one planter edge, in metres.
rows: Label the first bed side √36 and the second √64.
Find √36 = 6 m, since 6² = 36.
Find √64 = 8 m, since 8² = 64.
Find the planter edge ∛27 = 3 m, since 3³ = 27.
The bed perimeters are 4 × 6 = 24 m and 4 × 8 = 32 m.
Add lengths only: 24 + 32 + 3 = 59 m.
scenes.misconception: Convert two areas and one volume into lengths before adding; never add unlike units.

The first perimeter is 4 × 9 = 36 cm.
The second perimeter is 4 × 14 = 56 cm.
Subtract perimeters: 56 − 36 = 20 cm.

rows: A cube has three equal edges; V=s³.

Take ∛343=7 cm, because 7 × 7 × 7 = 343.
Compare edge lengths rather than subtracting volumes.
Subtract 7 − 4 = 3 cm.

rows: First evaluate the given side: 3²=9 cm.
Square that side to get the first area: 9 × 9=81 cm².
The other display already has area 144 cm².
Its side would be √144=12 cm; check 12²=144.
Subtract the smaller area from the larger: 144−81=63 cm².

scenes.problem: Compare 3³ with √64 × ∛27. By how much do the two values differ?
rows: Keep the power on the left and product of roots on the right.
Evaluate the left: 3³ = 27.
Evaluate √64 = 8; 8² = 64.
Evaluate ∛27 = 3; 3³ = 27.
Multiply the right: 8 × 3 = 24.
Compare 27 and 24; difference = 27 − 24 = 3.
scenes.misconception: Evaluate each power and root before comparing the two complete sides.

rows: Label the first bed side √100 and the second √169.
Find √100 = 10 m, since 10² = 100.
Find √169 = 13 m, since 13² = 169.
Find the planter edge ∛64 = 4 m, since 4³ = 64.
The bed perimeters are 4 × 10 = 40 m and 4 × 13 = 52 m.
Add lengths only: 40 + 52 + 4 = 96 m.
